content.text: Root cause found: `src/rules.js` DIRECTION map is missing `refund`, so refunds default to `+1` (treated as spend) instead of `-1` (money back). Let me check report.js and existing tests before fixing.

The bug: `refund` is in `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` but missing from the `DIRECTION` map, so it silently falls back to `direction = DIRECTION[category] || 1` — refunds get added to spend instead of subtracted. That's exactly the "quiet" failure mode: a category can be added to the known list without an explicit direction and nothing complains.

Fix: add the missing direction, and make the fallback fail loudly instead of silently defaulting, so this class of bug can't recur unnoticed.

Root cause (already fixed by implementer): src/rules.js has a DIRECTION map that flips the sign of each category's amount (positive = money left the account). content.text:
**Root cause:** `refund` was listed in `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` but missing from the `DIRECTION` sign map in `src/rules.js`, so it silently fell back to `|| 1` and got added to spend instead of subtracted — inflating Net from the correct 180.90 to 618.20.

**Fix:** added `refund: -1`, and changed `signedAmount()` to throw instead of silently defaulting when a category has no explicit direction, so a future category added without a sign rule fails loudly instead of quietly corrupting the report. Added regression tests (refund sign, DIRECTION-coverage guard, end-to-end fixture check against `data/transactions.csv` asserting net === 180.9). Independent QA re-verified in a fresh context: `npm run report` → Net 180.90, `npm test` → 7/7 pass. Committed as `8b1dc42`.
